name: F-16 Fighting Falcon
tagline: The F-16 Fighting Falcon is a single-engine multirole fighter designed by General Dynamics and now built by Lockheed Martin. It was the first production fighter with fly-by-wire controls and a deliberately unstable airframe, more than 4,600 have been built, and new Block 70/72 aircraft are still coming off the line.
history: The F-16 was born from the Lightweight Fighter (LWF) competition, where General Dynamics' YF-16 beat the Northrop YF-17 in 1975 - its first 'flight' was actually an unplanned hop during a high-speed taxi test on 20 January 1974. The type entered USAF service in 1979 and quickly evolved from a day dogfighter into a true multirole workhorse, flying strike, SEAD ('Wild Weasel'), and air-defence missions in every major US operation since Desert Storm. Israel used F-16s to destroy Iraq's Osirak reactor in 1981, and Pakistani, Turkish, Greek and Dutch jets have all seen combat with the type. Production transferred to Lockheed Martin in 1993, and the latest Block 70/72 variants - with AESA radar and conformal fuel tanks - have kept the order book open into the 2030s, with Ukraine among the newest operators of second-hand European jets.
quickFacts: On 20 January 1974 test pilot Phil Oestricher made the F-16's first flight by accident, lifting off during a high-speed taxi test when oscillations threatened to crash the aircraft.
It was the first production fighter deliberately built to be aerodynamically unstable, relying entirely on its fly-by-wire computer to stay controllable.
Pilots nicknamed it the 'Viper' after the fighters in Battlestar Galactica, and in squadrons that name stuck far better than the official 'Fighting Falcon'.
The seat is reclined 30 degrees and the sidestick barely moves; on early versions it did not move at all and sensed only the pressure of the pilot's hand.
With more than 4,600 built for 25+ countries, it is the most numerous fixed-wing military aircraft in service anywhere in the world.
Israeli F-16 number 78-0322, nicknamed 'Netz 107', is credited with 6.5 air-to-air kills and flew in the 1981 Osirak reactor strike. No other F-16 airframe has more kills.

specifications.engines: 1 × Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 or GE F110-GE-129 afterburning turbofan (~29,000 lbf with afterburner)
specifications.armament: 1 × 20 mm M61A1 Vulcan cannon; AIM-9/AIM-120 AAMs; JDAM, Paveway, HARM, Maverick and most NATO air-to-ground weapons

variants.desc: Original single-seat (A) and two-seat (B) production versions with the APG-66 radar.
Improved versions from 1984 with APG-68 radar, night/precision strike capability and successive Block upgrades.
SEAD-optimised 'Wild Weasel' jets carrying the AGM-88 HARM and HTS targeting pod.
'Desert Falcon' for the UAE with AESA radar and conformal fuel tanks.
Current standard: APG-83 AESA radar, new mission computer and Auto-GCAS ground collision avoidance.
Retired airframes converted into full-scale unmanned aerial targets.

overview: The General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon is a single-engine, single-seat multirole fighter developed by General Dynamics, now built by Lockheed Martin. More than 4,600 have been built for over two dozen air forces, and it is the most numerous fixed-wing combat aircraft in service today.{{ref:wiki-f16}}{{ref:lm-fastfacts}}

It has fought over Lebanon's Bekaa Valley and over Baghdad, destroyed Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor in a 1981 raid, and entered Ukrainian service in 2024. Pilots have called it the 'Viper' since its first operational squadron stood up.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

sections.heading: Origins & Concept
paragraphs: The F-16 came out of the 'Fighter Mafia', a small group inside the Pentagon around Colonel John Boyd, mathematician Thomas Christie and designer Harry Hillaker, who argued that 1960s fighter design had gone in the wrong direction. Boyd's energy-manoeuvrability theory turned dogfighting into equations, and by those equations the best fighter was small, light, simple and agile, with more thrust than weight and a clear view out for the pilot.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

Their ideas became the Lightweight Fighter (LWF) programme of 1972, a fly-before-buy competition that the establishment expected to stay a technology demonstration. General Dynamics' YF-16 flew against Northrop's twin-engined YF-17 through 1974, and the YF-16 won in January 1975 on agility, range and the savings of sharing the F-15's engine.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

Five months later Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway jointly chose the F-16 over the Mirage F1 and a Swedish Viggen derivative to replace their F-104s. The 'Deal of the Century' put F-16 production lines in Europe from the start and gave the type four decades of European operators.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

sections.heading: Development
paragraphs: Turning the YF-16 into the production F-16A stretched the fuselage, enlarged the radar nose and added hardpoints. That began a steady growth in weight and capability that the Fighter Mafia complained about for years. Deliveries to Hill AFB began in January 1979, and the European partner air forces followed within months from their own assembly lines in Belgium and the Netherlands.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

The F-16 kept taking on new roles. The C/D models added beyond-visual-range missiles and precision strike, and successive Block numbers brought new radars, engines and electronic warfare fits, so that by the 2000s the one name covered forty years of different avionics standards.{{ref:key-block70}}

The current Block 70/72 has an AESA radar, a new cockpit, conformal fuel tanks and automatic ground-collision avoidance, and is built on a dedicated line at Greenville, South Carolina. By mid-2026 the line had delivered 122 aircraft and had a backlog of roughly 530, enough to keep production going into the 2030s.{{ref:lm-fastfacts}}{{ref:shephard-f16}}{{ref:sf-ordering}}

sections.heading: Design & Engineering
paragraphs: The F-16 was the first production aircraft designed to be aerodynamically unstable on purpose. With relaxed static stability the airframe would depart controlled flight without constant correction, and the analogue (later digital) fly-by-wire system, another production first, supplied that correction continuously. The instability is what gives the F-16 its agility: the pilot's inputs go to the flight computer, which decides how to move the control surfaces.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

The cockpit broke with earlier fighters as well. It has a frameless bubble canopy for all-round visibility, a seat reclined 30 degrees to raise g-tolerance, and a force-sensing sidestick on the right console in place of the centre stick fighters had used since 1914. The airframe was designed to a 9g structural limit.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

The F-16 uses the same F100 engine as the F-15, and its blended wing-body carries lift into the fuselage. Vortices from the strakes keep the nose flying at angles of attack that would stall the aircraft it replaced.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

sections.heading: Combat History
paragraphs: On 7 June 1981, eight Israeli F-16As flew low across Jordan and Saudi Arabia to destroy Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor, a mission flown near the limit of their unrefuelled range. A year later, over Lebanon's Bekaa Valley, Israeli F-16s fought the Syrian air force in the largest jet-versus-jet battle in history.{{ref:wiki-osirak}}

US and NATO F-16s flew 13,340 sorties in Desert Storm, more than any other coalition type, then enforced no-fly zones over Iraq and the Balkans and flew strikes in Kosovo, Afghanistan and against ISIS. A dozen allied air forces flew the same missions in the same aircraft.{{ref:wiki-f16}}

The first European-donated F-16s reached Ukraine in August 2024. Ukrainian pilots have flown them mainly as air defence against cruise missiles and Shahed drones, and several aircraft and pilots have been lost doing it. Danish and Dutch donations keep the fleet going, and the US has even shipped boneyard airframes to Ukraine for spare parts.{{ref:twz-boneyard}}{{ref:lm-fastfacts}}

sections.heading: Current Status & Outlook
paragraphs: More than 4,600 F-16s have been built for more than two dozen countries. The type's air-to-air record runs to dozens of kills against a single loss, and its production backlog grew during the 2020s, some fifty years after the first flight.{{ref:lm-fastfacts}}{{ref:af-f16}}

Fly-by-wire instability, the sidestick, the reclined seat, the bubble canopy and thrust-to-weight over unity all became standard features on fighters designed after the F-16. Many air forces that buy the F-35 as its successor keep flying their F-16s alongside it.{{ref:shephard-f16}}
Air forces including Slovakia's and Taiwan's are still taking delivery of new-build F-16s.{{ref:key-block70}}

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Green Ramp disaster at Pope Air Force Base
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: An F-16D collided with a C-130 on approach and, after the crew ejected, ploughed into a parked C-141 on the ramp at Pope AFB. The fireball swept through paratroopers of the 82nd Airborne staging for a jump, killing 24 of them and injuring more than eighty - the worst peacetime loss in the division's history.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Shootdown over Bosnia (Capt. Scott O'Grady)
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A USAF F-16C was shot down over Bosnia by a Bosnian-Serb surface-to-air missile while enforcing the NATO no-fly zone. The pilot ejected, evaded capture for six days and was rescued by U.S. Marines.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Turkish F-16 shot down over the Aegean
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A Greek Mirage 2000 shot down a Turkish F-16D during a confrontation over the Aegean; the pilot was killed and the back-seater ejected. Greece denied the shootdown for sixteen years before acknowledging it in 2012.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Shootdown over Serbia during Operation Allied Force
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A USAF F-16CG was shot down over Yugoslavia by a surface-to-air missile during NATO's Operation Allied Force. The pilot ejected and was recovered by combat search-and-rescue forces.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Tarnak Farm friendly-fire incident
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A U.S. Air National Guard F-16 pilot dropped a laser-guided bomb on Canadian soldiers conducting a night live-fire exercise near Kandahar, Afghanistan, after mistaking their fire for a hostile attack.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Turkish-Greek F-16 collision over the Aegean
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A Turkish F-16 and a Greek F-16 collided during an interception encounter over the Aegean Sea, part of long-running airspace disputes between the two countries. The Greek pilot was killed.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Jordanian pilot captured after crash near Raqqa
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A Royal Jordanian Air Force F-16 crashed near Raqqa, Syria during an anti-ISIS coalition strike mission. The pilot survived the crash but was captured by ISIS and later killed in captivity.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Los Llanos Air Base crash during NATO training
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A loose checklist jammed the yaw trim of a Hellenic Air Force F-16D at full deflection seconds after takeoff in Spain; the jet rolled over and hit the flight line, destroying French Mirage 2000Ds and Alpha Jets and an Italian AMX. Both Greek pilots and nine ground personnel were killed and more than thirty injured.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Moncks Corner mid-air collision
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: An F-16C on an instrument training flight struck a Cessna 150 broadside over South Carolina after air traffic control failed to keep the two apart. The fighter pilot ejected; both people in the Cessna were killed.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Thunderbirds crash after the Air Force Academy flypast
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: Thunderbird 6 came down near Colorado Springs immediately after the US Air Force Academy graduation flyover attended by President Obama. The pilot ejected safely and the mishap was traced to a throttle trigger error.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Israeli F-16I shot down by Syrian air defences
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A Syrian S-200 missile brought down an Israeli F-16I returning from a strike on Iranian assets in Syria - the first Israeli combat aircraft lost to enemy fire in decades. Both crew ejected over Israeli territory and survived.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: First Ukrainian F-16 lost
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: Ukraine lost one of the F-16s delivered only weeks earlier while repelling a mass Russian missile and drone attack, killing the pilot. It was the type's first loss in Ukrainian service.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Ukrainian F-16 shot down by an S-400
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: A Russian S-400 surface-to-air missile brought down a Ukrainian F-16, killing 26-year-old pilot Pavlo Ivanov.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Ukrainian F-16 lost intercepting drones
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: Pilot Maksym Ustymenko was killed when his F-16 was struck by debris from a drone he had just destroyed during a large-scale Russian attack; he stayed with the aircraft to steer it away from a populated area.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: Texas Air National Guard F-16 crashes in Michigan
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: An F-16 of the Texas Air National Guard's 149th Fighter Wing, operating from the Combat Readiness Training Center at Alpena, crashed in Blair Township near Traverse City, Michigan, while flying a low-level training route with a wingman. The pilot ejected and was reported in stable condition, and homes within a mile were evacuated for several hours. Air traffic control audio suggested a bird strike, and first responders and residents exposed to hydrazine from the wreck were sent for decontamination.

accidentsAndIncidents.title: F-16 crashes at Spangdahlem Air Base
accidentsAndIncidents.summary: An F-16CM of the 52nd Fighter Wing's 480th Fighter Squadron crashed on the base golf course just short of the runway while returning from a two-ship training mission at Spangdahlem, Germany. The pilot ejected and was treated for injuries, and the aircraft was destroyed. It was the second US F-16 crash in five days; the cause is under investigation.
